text:
The Jets arrive in Montreal winless in nine (0-7-2), coming off a 7-0 loss at Carolina in which Pyotr Kochetkov stopped all 26 shots. They are outscored 37-16 over the stretch, and without Josh Morrissey (wrist) and Vladislav Namestnikov. The Canadiens have won five straight, though without Nick Suzuki and Ivan Demidov. With Suzuki out, Oliver Kapanen has taken his spot beside Slafkovský and Caufield, and Jake Evans is up to 17:04 a night.

Our numbers lean Montreal, 3.32 expected goals (the quality of chances) to 2.94. At five on five, the Canadiens have taken 53% of the expected goals to Winnipeg's 45%. The Canadiens take five penalties a game, so the Jets' power play will get looks. In net, Stuart Skinner (projected) is at +2.2 goals saved above expected this season, while Jacob Fowler (projected) is at +9.7, which is why Montreal's chances look only half as strong as its record. These teams met on Oct 25, and Montreal won 2-1.

Cole Caufield is our top Canadiens scorer at 39%, with Kyle Connor at 42% for Winnipeg. Our under-the-radar picks: Alexandre Texier of Montreal, on the third line but with 2.4 expected goals in his last 10 games (16% to score), and Cole Perfetti of the Jets, at 50% for a point because his line creates chances. Both are players to watch, not locks.
